\chapter{Verbs of Seeing and Saying}
\label{ch:ml-see-say}
\hlchaptermodality{44}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell someone to look, listen, speak and write in Malayalam.}

Complete ML-C44-write and say all four verbs in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[nōkkū]{\ml{നോക്കൂ} (nōkkū) — look}

\label{lesson:ML-C44-look}



\begin{quote}
Four verbs for taking things in and putting them out, one at a time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{നോക്കൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{നോക്കൂ}} (\emph{nōkkū}) — \textquotedblleft{}look\textquotedblright{}.

The same \emph{nōkk-} stem as Kannada's \emph{nōḍu}, with Malayalam's courteous long \emph{ū} on the end.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nōkkū}
  \item it once more, slowly
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{നോക്കൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}look\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kēḷkkū]{\ml{കേൾക്കൂ} (kēḷkkū) — listen}

\label{lesson:ML-C44-listen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nōkkū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കേൾക്കൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{കേൾക്കൂ}} (\emph{kēḷkkū}) — \textquotedblleft{}listen\textquotedblright{}.

And Kannada's \emph{kēḷu} again. Malayalam separated from Tamil later than the others, but this stem is older than any of the splits.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kēḷkkū}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item it after \emph{nōkkū}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കേൾക്കൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}listen\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[saṁsārikkū]{\ml{സംസാരിക്കൂ} (saṁsārikkū) — speak}

\label{lesson:ML-C44-speak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{kēḷkkū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സംസാരിക്കൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{സംസാരിക്കൂ}} (\emph{saṁsārikkū}) — \textquotedblleft{}speak\textquotedblright{}.

From Sanskrit \emph{saṁsāra} — literally 'going around together'. The everyday Malayalam word for conversing is a Sanskrit compound, which is how much of the language's formal vocabulary arrived.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{saṁsārikkū}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item it after \emph{kēḷkkū}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സംസാരിക്കൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}speak\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[eḻutū]{\ml{എഴുതൂ} (eḻutū) — write}

\label{lesson:ML-C44-write}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{saṁsārikkū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{എഴുതൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{എഴുതൂ}} (\emph{eḻutū}) — \textquotedblleft{}write\textquotedblright{}.

From \emph{eḻuttu}, 'letter' — the writing verb is built from the thing written, which is the reverse of how Kannada does it.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
That closes the run: look, listen, speak, write.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{eḻutū}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item it after \emph{saṁsārikkū}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{എഴുതൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}write\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
